experiments.name: Freelancer comparison-page test
experiments.hypothesis: A freelancer-specific comparison page linked to a client-intake template will turn qualified visits into free signups.
experiments.population: Freelancers reaching the new page through existing site links, search, or other unpaid referrals.
experiments.primaryMetric: Free signups per qualified page visit; also record published forms and paid accounts.
guardrails: Keep competitor comparisons dated, fair, and fact-checked.
Confirm the template link and signup attribution work before launch.
Do not expand to another audience without the stated scale conditions.
experiments.stoppingRule: Target 500 qualified visits by day 90; at the supplied 2% planning assumption, that is about 10 free signups, not a forecast. At 500 visits, below 1% signup means stop or rewrite; 1% to below 2% means revise once. Expand only if signup rate is at least 2%, at least one paid account is attributable, and measured 12-month gross profit supports full campaign cost. If traffic is below 500 at day 90, label results directional and do not infer failure.

experiments.name: Feature-triggered Pro email
experiments.hypothesis: A relevant email sent after a user tries to add a Pro feature can produce attributable paid upgrades.
experiments.population: Free users who try to add payments or another Pro feature and can lawfully receive the message.
experiments.primaryMetric: Paid upgrades attributable to delivered emails within 90 days; clicks are the leading indicator.
guardrails: Do not email users without a lawful basis; retain unsubscribe handling.
Pause if consent or delivery problems appear.
Do not treat a smaller-than-500 cohort as evidence of failure.
experiments.stoppingRule: Aim for 500 eligible sends only if that many users exist; otherwise send to the eligible cohort and label results directional. At 500 sends, zero clicks stops this email approach. At day 90, no attributable paid account also stops it. Scale only after an attributable upgrade and evidence that 12-month gross profit supports the full campaign cost, including owner time.

output.diagnosis: The constraint is unverified unit economics: price is known, but gross margin, free-to-paid conversion, and customer-source data are not. That makes paid CAC unsafe to set; this diagnosis is wrong if existing cohort data already shows reliable paid conversion and payback below three months.
output.affordableCac: Assumption: 60% gross margin per Pro seat, to validate in week one. At a three-month ceiling: $6 × 60% × 3 = $10.80 per paid seat; the account ceiling is $10.80 multiplied by paid seats. Keep total acquisition cost, including owner time, below the validated limit; do not buy ads until actual margin and conversion data support it.

plays.name: Feature-triggered Pro email
plays.oneLiner: Show free users the relevant Pro feature when their form needs it.
plays.audience: Existing Formkit free users who try to add payments or another Pro feature; run only if this cohort can be identified and lawfully emailed.
plays.trigger: A free user reaches for a Pro feature, such as payments through their own Stripe account.
plays.hook: Need payments on your form? Pro is $6 per seat per month, and payments go to your Stripe account. Formkit takes no cut.
plays.mechanic: Send one behavior-triggered email and track delivered messages, clicks, and paid upgrades. MailerLite reports a 2.09% average email campaign click rate [mailerlite.com, grade A]; treat this as a directional benchmark, not a Formkit lifecycle result.
plays.assetUsed: Formkit’s free tier, Stripe payment support with no Formkit cut, and $6-per-seat Pro plan.
funnel: Emails sent: 500 test target, sized to yield about 10 clicks at the 2.09% benchmark; no eligible cohort size is confirmed.
Email sent → click: 1.5% low / 2.09% likely / 3% high; likely rate from MailerLite [mailerlite.com, grade A]; low and high are planning assumptions, grade D.
Click → paid account: 0.5% low / 1% likely / 3% high; assumption, grade D. No Formkit click-to-paid rate was supplied.
plays.biggestUnknown: Whether enough eligible free users exist and what share of email clicks become paid accounts.
plays.test: If at least 500 eligible users exist, send one email and track upgrades for 90 days. Platform spend: $0. Allow two owner hours, valued at $50/hour as an assumption ($100). If the cohort is smaller, test only the available cohort and treat results as directional.
plays.killIf: Stop this email approach if 500 sends produce zero clicks, or if the 90-day cohort produces no attributable paid account. Do not infer failure from a smaller cohort.
plays.scaleIf: Scale only after an attributable paid account and a calculated 12-month gross profit per account that exceeds the full campaign cost, including owner time. The $6 seat price alone is not enough to establish payback.
plays.firstActionToday: Check whether product analytics can identify free users who tried to use payments or another Pro feature.
plays.climbosCanDo: Draft the email, define the cohort and tracking events, and report clicks and paid upgrades.

plays.name: Freelancer Google Forms switcher page
plays.oneLiner: Link Formkit’s existing comparison content to a freelancer client-intake template.
plays.audience: Freelancers comparing form builders, reached through Formkit’s comparison page and search traffic.
plays.trigger: A freelancer’s basic form no longer fits their client intake or branding needs.
plays.hook: Build a client intake form that fits your workflow. Start free; upgrade when you need Pro features.
plays.mechanic: Use a fair, dated alternative page and link a relevant starter template. The supplied SaaS B2B play research reports a 1–5% planning range for alternative-page signups, based on vendor reports [eesel.ai; tripledart.com, grade C]. The same research gives 50–2,000 visits per niche page per month as a practitioner estimate, grade D; it is not a Formkit traffic forecast.
plays.assetUsed: Formkit’s existing comparison page and template library, identified in the research notes: https://formkit.app/ and https://formkit.app/templates.
funnel: Qualified page visits: 500 test target, chosen to produce about 10 free signups at the 2% likely planning rate; achieving this traffic in 90 days is unverified.
Qualified visit → free signup: 1% low / 2% likely / 5% high; planning range from the SaaS B2B play research [eesel.ai; tripledart.com, grade C]. The 2% likely rate is an assumption within that range.
Free signup → paid account: 0.5% low / 1% likely / 3% high; assumption, grade D. No Formkit free-to-paid rate was supplied.
plays.unit: Paid accounts from 500 qualified page visits
plays.biggestUnknown: Whether the page can attract 500 qualified visits during the test and how many signups become paid accounts.
plays.test: Update one page and link one relevant template. Target 500 qualified visits within 90 days; allow up to five owner hours, valued at $50/hour as an assumption ($250). No ad spend. Track visits, free signups, and paid accounts separately.
plays.killIf: At 500 qualified visits, stop or rewrite the page if free signups are below 1%, the low end of the cited planning range. Check paid outcomes through day 90 before judging conversion.
plays.scaleIf: Expand to another audience only if free signups reach at least the 2% planning rate, at least one paid account is attributable to the page, and measured 12-month gross profit supports the owner-time cost.
plays.firstActionToday: Open Formkit’s existing comparison page and select the freelancer intake template to link.
plays.climbosCanDo: Review the comparison page for factual accuracy, draft the template link and CTA, and set up source-level conversion tracking.

output.portfolioNote: Run one bankable lifecycle-email test and one creative comparison-page test. Neither has proven paid conversion; keep paid-media spend at $0 until actual customer economics support acquisition cost.
